messages:
Priya: Quick design pass on roles grid + invite confirm. Two quick asks: 1) a compact mode for dense role tables (useful for admins managing lots of teams), 2) clearer wording on the invite confirmation when SSO is required. Figma: https://redwood.ai/figma/rbac-compact

Jon: Compact mode 👍. We should collapse the permissions column into a hover/expand so rows stay single-line. Maybe show a chevron that expands an in-row mini-panel with checkmarks.

Arun: Agree on collapse. Accessibility note: expanded in-row panels need proper aria-controls and keyboard toggle. Make sure screen readers announce "expanded" and the panel id.

Maya: Invite confirm copy currently: "Invite will be sent. Recipients must use SSO if enabled." Sounds a bit clunky. Two variants:
- terse: "Invites sent. SSO required."
- explanatory: "Invites sent. Recipients must sign in with your organizations SSO."
Which should we use? Terse fits compact UI but may confuse non-technical admins.

Priya: Let's default to explanatory, and show the terse line in compact mode with an info tooltip linking to a short explainer. Tooltip text: 'Users will authenticate via your org SSO; you can manage SSO in Organization settings.'

Jon: Small UX: when SSO enforcement is on, surface a badge in the top-right of the invite drawer: 'SSO enforced'. Badge should be color-coded and keyboard-focusable to open the explainer tooltip.

Arun: Also flag for devs: audit log should emit an accessible live region update when invites are sent so screen reader users know actions completed. Eg. aria-live="polite" with message '3 invites sent'.

DesignBot: Uploaded compact-grid prototype v1: in-row chevrons, hover summary for permissions, SSO badge in invite drawer, explanatory copy on confirm. Accessibility checklist updated: aria-controls on chevrons, aria-expanded states, live region for invite events.

Maya: One more: pagination in audit UI is currently page-based. For review workflows, infinite scroll with a 'jump to time' quick filter is better. Propose adding a 'Jump to date' control + keyboard shortcuts (kbd: `j t`) to open it.

Priya: Sounds good. I'll update the mocks and add copy for the explainer page. Thanks all :sparkles:
